newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch Schiphol says passengers, freight up in H1.
newsitem.headline: Dutch Schiphol says passengers, freight up in H1.

text.p: Amsterdam Airport Schiphol said on Thursday passenger handling and freight throughput in the first half of 1996 both rose significantly year-on-year.
"In the first six months Schiphol handled 12.8 million passengers (+9.4 percent) and 530,000 tonnes of freight (+11.8 percent)," the airport said in a statement.
The upturn in traffic and transport volumes boosted revenues from airport charges by 10.7 percent to 203.6 million guilders ($122.6 million).
First-half net profit mushroomed 40.3 percent to 78.7 million guilders from a year-earlier 56.1 million.
But Schiphol said revenues from concessions were braked by the separation between Schengen (border-free) and non-Schengen passengers at the airport, which depressed tax-free sales.
However, income from concessions was expected to pick up in the second half, it added.
For the full year the airport has upgraded its profit forecast, saying it expects a "substantial rise" in the net result. In April the company said it expected a further improvement in net profits.
The airport said investments over full-1996 were expected to total some 325 million guilders.
